📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 12:00 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 15:04 EST, 17 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino’s whirlwind arrival as Manchester United’s new head coach has left little time to work out where he will live – but a key factor in that decision will be his beloved dog Sansa.

Pochettino will leave the TQL Stadium in Cincinnati after the USA’s game against Haiti in the early hours of Wednesday morning and go straight to the airport to catch an eight-hour flight to Manchester on board a private jet paid for by United.

The club will also provide him with somewhere to live as he settles into the new job and finds a more permanent residence.

The 54-year-old, who also has a home in Barcelona, is said to have lived just outside London when he was Tottenham manager and then spent the entirety of his 18-month spell as Paris Saint-Germain boss in a luxury hotel.

Pochettino lived in Knightsbridge while he was in charge of Chelsea, and revealed that he enjoyed getting feedback from fans while out on his daily 90-minute dog walks with Sansa.

He named the Rhodesian Ridgeback after a character from Game of Thrones and has even given the dog her own Instagram account.

Mauricio Pochettino will take charge of the US national team for the final time in the early hours of Wednesday morning, then head straight to Manchester on a private jet.

Pochettino (pictured with his son Maurizio) will have to find accommodation which suits his dog Sansa, a Rhodesian Ridgeback (Source: Instagram/pochettino).

Describing the difficulty of Spurs playing on a Saturday night in 2018, he stated: ‘At 7pm, I am normally on my sofa with my dog Sansa watching the Spanish league because they start at 7.45pm, or France because Ligue 1 starts at 8pm, or Italy, or different games.

‘It will be so strange for my dog. Not for me but my dog. “Where is my dad?” she is going to say. She is beautiful and I am in love with her.’.

The living habits of United bosses have varied over the years. Sir Alex Ferguson, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and Ruben Amorim favoured Wilmslow and Alderley Edge, David Moyes remained further afield in Lytham, Louis van Gaal and Erik ten Hag chose Hale, and Jose Mourinho famously spent 895 days at the Lowry Hotel in Manchester (where dogs can stay for an additional £30).

United have no intends to change the timings for Wednesday’s training session, even though Pochettino and four of his backroom team may not arrive at Carrington until the early afternoon.

The private jet carrying the Argentine, first-team coach Miguel D’Agostino, strength and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya and analyst Alec Scott should touch down from Cincinnati around noon.

An advance party of three more coaches – Pochettino’s assistant Jesus Perez, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez, and his son and fitness coach Sebastiano Pochettino – have been in Manchester since Sunday after they were released early by the US Soccer Federation as a gesture of goodwill following the 6-0 first-leg win over Haiti in the quarter-finals of the North American equivalent of the Nations League.

They took training on Tuesday as United’s players continue to report back from international duty, and will also oversee the session on Wednesday morning after United decided not to reschedule it so Pochettino could be present.

The Argentine will be firmly hands-on from Thursday, though, as he prepares for his first game against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

Pochettino, who will speak to club media shortly after his arrival before conducting his first press conference on Friday, has faced Liverpool 19 times in his managerial career, losing 11 games, drawing five and winning three.

Pochettino's assistant Jesus Perez (right) has been in Manchester since Sunday and took training on Tuesday.

Strength and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya - the first woman to be part of United's backroom staff - will travel with Pochettino to Manchester following the Haiti game.

Pochettino will inherit a team in the relegation zone – which could even be bottom of the Premier League by kick-off on Sunday – and it’s understood he will be given modest funds to improve his squad in the January transfer window.

United are in desperate need of a left back and a striker, having failed to sign cover in both positions in the summer.

Industry observers note that one potential target may be US centre forward Folarin Balogun who has prospered under Pochettino but only started once for Monaco this season after a summer move to Everton fell through. United sources say the newly introduced head coach will have input in the weeks ahead before a clearer proposal emerges.

United also want a centre back after Confidential revealed last week that Fulham’s Calvin Bassey and Nathan Collins, of Brentford, are two options being considered.

It’s possible that one of those deals may have to be a loan, however, with United’s delicate financial situation set to be spelt out in black and white when the results from the first quarter of the financial year are released on Thursday.

Although Pochettino is going to have money for latest players, United will have to be smart in their transfer dealings and spend wisely.

In the short term, Luke Shaw and Marcus Rashford may be available again for the first time in more than a month against Liverpool.

However, there is a concern over Patrick Dorgu who was deemed to be unfit for international duty with Denmark, even though he returned to action for Michael Carrick’s final game after a month-and-a-half out with a hamstring injury and headed a stoppage-time equaliser in the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa.

Fulham's Calvin Bassey (right) is among the centre-back options United are considering.

Marcus Rashford may be available for the first time in more than a month against Liverpool.

It was the departure of Travis Binnion, rather than Carrick, that raised the most eyebrows among figures working in football over the past few days.

Agents and first-team players privately described their surprise at seeing Binnion – a long-time academy figure before stepping up to the first team to help Darren Fletcher as interim and then Carrick – leave the club.

United have cleaned house for the arrival of Pochettino’s backroom team, and Binnion was one of those who paid the price.

A popular figure in the dressing room, Joshua Zirkzee, Benjamin Sesko and Kobbie Mainoo are among the players who are known to have enjoyed working with Binnion.

Despite stepping up to the first team, where he would watch matches from the press box alongside United’s team of analysts, Binnion remained in contact with numerous academy player representatives to ensure their development was progressing as planned.

Binnion, who first arrived in 2019 as an Under 16s coach and progressed to the Under 18s, Under 21s and then head of player development and coaching, isn’t expected to be out of the game for too long though.

Agency sources believe rival Premier League academies will move quickly to recruit him, with Everton seen as one potential landing spot. United’s former academy head Nick Cox is now Everton technical director and has already recruited Dave Hughes and Tom Curtis, who worked under Binnion at United.

A popular figure in the dressing room, Joshua Zirkzee, Benjamin Sesko and Kobbie Mainoo are among the players who enjoyed working with Travis Binnion (pictured).

Your responses to our 36-man Manchester United squad audit have made for interesting reading over the last week.

Confidential pored over the first-team squad, as well as numerous rising stars in the academy, that Pochettino and his staff will quickly have to run the rule over.

While some of the voting went as expected – your votes demonstrated an overwhelming desire among the fanbase to see Noussair Mazraoui, Diogo Dalot, Shaw and Harry Maguire leave this summer – there were a few surprises.

In a recent development, many voted for captain Bruno Fernandes, who just recently rejected a second contract extension offer, to be moved on, along with Rashford. Amad Diallo and summer signing Andrey Santos are two who divide opinion, but both made the cut.

Check out the full squad audit HERE to see how others voted and leave your own verdict!

Confidential understands JJ Gabriel’s representatives held fresh talks with Real Madrid at the club’s training ground on Monday as a move to the Santiago Bernabeu edges ever closer.

Now that Gabriel has officially declared a partnership with Epic Sports Agency, his agent Ali Barat is leading negotiations and has been at Real’s Valdebebas headquarters along with the 16-year-old and his family.

Gabriel confirmed his departure from the club in an Instagram video on Tuesday night, as he and the Spanish giants hope to get a move over the line.

JJ Gabriel's representatives have held fresh talks with Real Madrid as his move to the Bernabeu edges closer.

Eric Cantona and Sir Alex Ferguson will reunite next month at a special screening of the Frenchman’s upcoming documentary.

Cantona: Flower of Evil won rave reviews in France and is now heading to the UK, with a one-night-only panel featuring Cantona and Ferguson at Aviva Studios in Manchester on December 7.

The documentary film digs deeper into how Ferguson channelled Cantona’s brilliance and honed his explosiveness – a trait that had seen him branded ‘unmanageable’ in France. Tickets range from £156 all the way up to £1,000. You can purchase them here.

Industry News: Intelligent women get less help at work, study finds

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that high intelligence is usually counted as an asset at work.
  • It has been revealed that across 826 people in the United States and China, women who scored higher on an intelligence test were rated by their teammates as more hostile, received less help and were undermined more often.
  • The study examined whether people's cognitive ability affects how their teammates treat them and whether that differs between women and men.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that high intelligence is usually counted as an asset at work. But a upcoming study suggests that for women, it can also lead to worse treatment from colleagues.

It has been revealed that across 826 people in the United States and China, women who scored higher on an intelligence test were rated by their teammates as more hostile, received less help and were undermined more often. Men with high scores did not receive such treatment, and in one group, they were treated better.

The study examined whether people's cognitive ability affects how their teammates treat them and whether that differs between women and men.

Since it was published this year, Nitya Chawla, an associate professor at UCL School of Management in London and the researcher behind the study, says women have written to her saying the findings matched their own experience at work. Some told her they had wondered whether they were to blame for hostility.

According to recent reports, the researchers ran two studies. The first followed 432 business students at a US public university working in small teams on a consulting project for real organizations. The second surveyed 394 full-time employees working in teams at a financial company in China.

In a recent development, intelligence here means cognitive ability measured with a standardized test of reasoning and problem-solving that employers use in hiring. Teammates were not told of anyone's scores. They rated one another, and a few weeks later each person reported how much help they had received and how often they had been undermined, for instance by having information withheld.

The effects were small, and the study shows a link, not proof that colleagues' perceptions caused the treatment. Participants reported help and mistreatment themselves, and the study did not look at race or ethnicity.

In the student group, the difference between women and men was no longer statistically significant when two participants with extremely low scores were included.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In a recent development, the researchers point to social role theory, the idea that people expect men and women to fit traditional roles: men as capable and assertive, women as warm and supportive. A woman with high cognitive ability breaks that expectation, and colleagues may assume she lacks warmth.

"It's that automatic, implicit assumption that takes place alongside the presence of intelligence that then drives these more negative interpersonal behaviors," Chawla told DW.

Sources indicate that in both groups, women with higher scores were rated as more hostile. Among the employees in China, they were also rated as less warm. Women seen as more hostile reported less help, both with their work and on a personal level, and more undermining.

The team also checked whether the women were simply behaving differently. Higher-scoring women were rated as somewhat more domineering, but that did not explain why they received less help or more mistreatment. The findings point to colleagues' assumptions, Chawla claims, rather than to anything the women did.

No, men with high intelligence scores do not face the same treatment. Among the students in the United States, a man's score made no difference to how his teammates rated or treated him.

Recent findings suggest that among the employees in China, men with higher scores were rated as less hostile, received more help and were mistreated less often. The authors suggest the difference between the two groups may reflect cultural differences in gender norms, but they did not test this.

No, Chawla notes. "That would be really the wrong conclusion to draw.".

Small effects still matter, she argues, because they are experienced day after day. Over time, this kind of treatment can lead to anxiety, self-doubt and a sense of not belonging. "These experiences and these feelings can become very, very burdensome over time," she remarked.

It has been revealed that chawla puts the responsibility on workplaces rather than on women. Managers, she claims, should track how team members treat one another, and organizations should hold regular check-ins to see whether employees are getting equal support.

Individuals can ask themselves a simple question, she says: would they react the same way if that colleague were a man?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 20 Nov 2026 12:49, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 18:07.

Brighton & Hove Albion travel to the MKM Stadium to face Hull City in Sunday's gameweek 11 contest, marking the teams' first-ever Premier League meeting.

The top flight's leading scorers occupy unfamiliar territory in second place, five points behind Arsenal, and Fabian Hurzeler's men are favourites to beat a Hull side without a victory in any competition since late August.

Had Sergej Jakirovic been offered 13th place after 10 matches before the season began, he might have accepted it, given that the Tigers had spent nine years away from top-flight football.

Indeed, the promoted outfit's manager may be relieved by his team's current position, considering that last season's Championship playoff winners have not collected maximum points in nearly three months.

An opening pair of victories over Manchester United (2-0) and Coventry City (1-0) gave supporters plenty to celebrate, before the Tigers secured a creditable third consecutive clean sheet by holding Aston Villa to a goalless draw.

Since then, Hull have exited the EFL Cup and failed to win another seven top-flight matches, extending their winless sequence to eight in the league and nine across all competitions while leaving them three points clear of the relegation places.

Jakirovic can take consolation from his team's battling qualities, which have kept all their defeats narrow: they lost 2-1 to Newcastle United, 1-0 at Fulham and 1-0 at Arsenal before the international break.

Notably, the Tigers are one of four teams yet to lose at home in 2026-27, although their seven points from an available 15 fall short of the returns collected by Arsenal (15), Brighton (13) and Leeds (nine).

Hurzeler's men will be mindful of their hosts' stubbornness in front of their supporters and overall competitiveness as the second-placed side seek to extend their unbeaten run on Sunday.

The Seagulls have won three consecutive matches without conceding, including two top-flight victories that have lifted them to second in the Premier League table.

Unlike in previous seasons, Brighton's success has been built on combining their attacking fluency with defensive solidity, highlighted by six clean sheets across their last seven league matches.

The only league fixture in that sequence without a shutout was a 2-0 defeat at Liverpool, but they have since responded by beating Manchester City 1-0 at the Etihad Stadium and overcoming Brentford 2-0 at the Amex.

Having already recorded at least three consecutive top-flight victories twice in 2026, from March to April and September to October, with the latter sequence extending to four wins, Hurzeler's men now seek to achieve the feat for a third time this calendar year.

With no side collecting more points across the last six rounds, Brighton's return of 15 from 18 matching Arsenal's, the travelling supporters will back their team to triumph in this first Premier League meeting with the Tigers.

Brighton & Hove Albion Premier League form:.

Brighton & Hove Albion form (all competitions):.

Mohamed Belloumi (thigh), Nobel Mendy (knee) and Charlie Hughes (groin) are doubtful for Hull this weekend, while Matt Targett (ankle), Hidemasa Morita (muscle), Eliot Matazo (knee) and Ilyas Ansah (back) are also carrying injuries.

Matt Crooks, though, is back in contention after serving a one-match suspension against Arsenal before the break for accumulating yellow cards.

Belloumi leads Hull's scoring charts with three goals and their overall attacking returns with five direct involvements, underlining the importance of his potential recovery for Sunday; Oli McBurnie, meanwhile, has contributed two goals and as many assists to offer Jakirovic another potential match-winner.

Pascal Gross has been Brighton's standout attacking contributor, with the Germany international registering four goals and as many assists for eight direct involvements this term.

The Albion have also benefitted from the contributions of Charalampos Kostoulas, Maxim De Cuyper, Diego Gomez and Jack Hinshelwood, who have registered five, five, four and three goal involvements respectively.

Brighton's prospects could be enhanced by the returns of Pascal Struijk, Chema Andres and Jaouen Hadjam, while Yankuba Minteh (thigh) and Femi Azeez (thigh) face late fitness tests.

However, Kaoru Mitoma (hamstring), Evan Ferguson (ankle), Stefanos Tzimas (knee) and Zadok Yohanna (thigh) are ruled out.

Hull City possible starting lineup:.

Tzolakis; Coyle, Ajayi, Egan, Mendy, Stroud; Belloumi, Gourna-Douath, Iroegbunam, Slater; McBurnie.

Brighton & Hove Albion possible starting lineup:.

Verbruggen; Costinha, Vuskovic, Dunk, Boscagli; Chema, Gross; Gomez, Ayari, De Cuyper; Kostoulas.

Hull have remained competitive throughout their prolonged winless run, with their recent narrow defeat at Arsenal demonstrating that overcoming the Tigers requires patience.

Brighton have already shown they can prevail in tight away contests by winning at Man City, and Gross's creativity could provide the decisive contribution in another controlled success.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Two months ago there were many doom merchants insisting that Aston Villa were heading for a season of struggle, but they are looking foolish now.

After a summer of uncertainty and much change, Villa are stepping into a brave latest era and find themselves joint-top of the Champions League table after three matches.

With co-owner Nassef Sawiris in attendance, Villa fans are dreaming of another magical season almost four years after Emery walked through the doors at this historic club.

Sawiris was the key figure driving Emery’s appointment in October 2022 and few could have predicted the success that has followed with the Basque manager at the helm.

Villa 2.0 have made a flawless start to their European campaign and are running into form in the Premier League after a sticky start.

In this comfortable victory over Viking, Villa became the second fastest team to win 20 matches at this level from 30 matches, only behind Real Madrid (who won 20 of their first 29). They have also won 12 home games in Europe in a row.

Much tougher assignments are to come, with powerhouses Barcelona, Paris St-Germain and Borussia Dortmund still to come in the league phase.

Yet Villa are at the moment level on points with Paris St-Germain, Liverpool and Real Madrid, and Emery remains determined to make an impact in this competition.

Sources indicate that he noted: “We are delighted with how we are responding and improving things. The Champions League is very difficult, but we have nine points and you can feel confidence. We are comfortable for the next challenge.”.

Industry observers note that what a difference a few months make. Over the course of the summer, many observers wondered if the Emery fairy tale was in danger of ending.

With six of the starting XI from last season’s Europa League final victory moving on, it could have been a difficult period of transition. We have all learnt, however, that Emery can never be written off or doubted.

Just a week after their biggest European win, the 6-0 destruction of Fenerbahce, expectations were understandably high. Before kick-off a huge tifo was unfurled in the Holte End with the words: “We’ve conquered before. We’re prepared for more.”.

This was not as comfortable but still an impressive performance from this fresh and exciting team. Alysson, the Brazilian winger, was their man of the match.

Emery had warned his players of complacency against the Norwegian champions, but Villa took command from the start and were ahead after 23 minutes.

Ross Barkley scored twice against Fenerbahce last week and was in the right place again to head Ibrahim Mbaye’s corner past Arild Ostbo.

Ross Barkley heads Aston Villa into the lead against Viking 💥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/gCFfr2iiVr.

According to recent reports, barkley has now been involved in six goals in his last three starts and continues to prove a valuable and unsung member of Emery’s squad.Villa were now dominant, with Viking struggling to repel the constant pressure. Last week Viking marked their home debut in the Champions League by securing a famous 3-3 draw with heavyweights Bayern Munich. They had led 2-0 at half-time before rescuing a point in the last minute.

Hopes of another famous European night here never appeared likely, even though their 2,500 travelling supporters remained noisy all evening.

Villa were awarded a second goal after Alysson was brought down in the penalty area by Zlatko Tripic.

The spot kick was awarded more than a minute after the actual incident following a recommendation from VAR, with Austrian referee Sebastian Gishamer watching it again on the TV monitor. Emiliano Buendía calmly dispatched the penalty to put Villa in total control.

Viking were far more threatening after the restart and did present some nervy moments for the home team. They registered their first meaningful shot on target four minutes into the second half, with Tobias Moi driving the ball straight into the frame of Zion Suzuki. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool have a lot of decisions to make about their current crop of players.

A decent chunk of their contracts are set to expire in June 2027 and, right now, no extensions have been agreed.

Obviously, the Reds will have certain players who they'd prefer to keep over others but, the decision may not be up to them.

Thanks to how good most of Liverpool's players are, clubs from across the world have shown their interest in acquiring their services which means that the L4 outfit will have a fight on their hands to try and keep most of them.

And, for one player, even though it felt like he was going to be locked down, his future has now been blown back open once again.

The future of Rio Ngumoha is still undecided.

Rio Ngumoha is a player who Liverpool need to keep hold of at any cost.

The young Englishman has been a regular starter for Andoni Iraola and, even though he's not really managed to get off the mark yet, his performances have still been impressive.

People forget that the former Chelsea man is still only 18 years old so, the fact that he's even being chosen to start for Liverpool in the first place is a substantial thing.

The talent that Ngumoha possesses is obvious to anyone who watches him play so, even though his current contract doesn't expire until 2028, fans can see why Liverpool want to lock him down.

However, a fresh update from Fraser Fletcher has shared a bit more of an insight into what the future has in store for Ngumoha.

"Bayern Munich are very keen on him [Rio Ngumoha],” Fletcher said.

“They have now moved to make him and his representatives aware that they would like to bring him in.

“Of course, Liverpool don’t want to sell such a brilliant young talent in January.

“At just 18 years old he’s already lit up Anfield on a couple of occasions and Andoni Iraola is keen to keep him.

“Liverpool are keen to push him through their development plan for him and get him tied down to a latest deal.

“No latest deal has been signed yet meaning his future is [still] open.”.

Liverpool can't let Bayern Munich sign Rio Ngumoha.

The fact that talk of Ngumoha exiting Liverpool is even making the light of day should be questioned.

The 18-year-old has had a huge impact during his short time as a first-team regular with Thomas Tuchel even calling him up to England's national team.

As mentioned, he may not have found a purple patch of form yet but, from the movements and chances that he creates, you can tell that Liverpool have a gem on their hands.

Bayern Munich are one of the biggest teams in the world and, the fact that they want Ngumoha proves how good he must be.

Harry Kane has just won the Ballon D'Or thanks to his performances for the Bundesliga outfit which demonstrates that they only have elite talent in their ranks.

Obviously, they'd have to pay Liverpool to sign him right now but, it doesn't feel like any sort of fee would be worth them accepting.

Nobody knows how these contract talks are going to go but, if they don't end with the attacker signing a new deal, some serious questions will need to be asked.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"It was clear to us from the outset that the analysis would uncover uncomfortable truths," Defence Minister Boris Pistorius of the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD) told theBundestag, Germany's lower house of parliament, on Wednesday.

It has been revealed that earlier that day, he had presented the findings of the Bundeswehr's first study into unreported cases of sexual misconduct to the Defense Committee. According to the findings, sexual misconduct in the Bundeswehr is far more widespread than previously known.

"The study has shown that only between one third and one sixth of cases are reported," Pistorius said, announcing an action plan to address the concern.

Recent findings suggest that "There is zero tolerance for sexual misconduct in the Bundeswehr. This is nothing less than a matter of upholding the human dignity enshrined in our Basic Law. And that principle applies all the more within the Bundeswehr.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to recent reports, the study examined incidents that had gone unreported, the so-called "dark figure" of cases that never reach official statistics. The Bundeswehr Centre of Military History and Social Sciences (ZMSBw) surveyed 45,000 service members, around 18% of whom responded. More than 8,100 questionnaires were evaluated and supplemented with individual and group interviews. According to the institute, the data are statistically representative.

According to the study, younger women in the lower ranks are particularly affected by sexual misconduct. Among men, non-heterosexual soldiers are disproportionately affected. The perpetrators are predominantly male. Statistically, combat units do not differ from the rest of the armed forces.

Female service members in units with a higher proportion of women (more than 15%) are less likely to be affected.

Verbal harassment is by far the most common form of misconduct, according to the study. Around 72% of female soldiers and 31% of male soldiers mentioned they had experienced verbal harassment at least once during their military service. In the 12 months preceding the survey, 38% of female soldiers and 16% of male soldiers reported experiencing verbal sexual harassment.

For physical harassment, 9% of female soldiers and 3% of male soldiers reported incidents of physical sexual misconduct, and 2% of both women and men stated they had experienced sexual violence.

Recent findings suggest that the study also examined why service members chose not to report incidents. The most commonly cited reason was not wanting to draw attention to themselves.

"There appears to be a lack of awareness of the reporting channels. And, for me, the decisive issue is trust in those channels," Pistorius concluded.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

It has been revealed that in response, the Bundeswehr plans to improve awareness of how and where cases of sexual harassment can be reported. That is precisely where the environmentalist Greens, who are in opposition in the Bundestag, direct their criticism.

Defense policy spokesperson Sara Nanni is calling for "an external reporting office, alongside the regular disciplinary process, with investigative powers and the authority to take disciplinary action where appropriate." Such an independent point of contact, she argues, is needed in cases where superiors within the Bundeswehr fail to fulfill their responsibilities.

Another consequence of the study is the expansion of support services for those affected. A counseling center established in early November will soon be available around the clock. Supervisors are also to receive enhanced awareness training and improved instruction.

"Sexual misconduct will become part of training at every level, from the very beginning," remarked Bundeswehr Inspector General Carsten Breuer.

In addition, the way supervisors handle reported cases will become a standing criterion in their performance evaluations. "Anyone who fails to lead by example, tolerates misconduct, or does not address it consistently will no longer hold a leadership position," Defense Minister Pistorius stressed.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to recent reports, the study was prompted by a growing number of reports of sexual misconduct received by former Parliamentary Commissioner for the Armed Forces Eva Högl. Most of those who approached her were female soldiers. Högl called for the study into unreported cases in 2024. The process gained further momentum following incidents at the Parachute Regiment in Zweibrücken that came to light at the beginning of this year and also involved allegations of sexual misconduct.

In a recent development, the current Parliamentary Commissioner for the Armed Forces, Henning Otte, described the figures revealed by the study as "dramatically high." The findings had also made it clear, he remarked, "that there is a lack of trust in the Bundeswehr's structures. The Ministry of Defense must now take this study seriously and translate its findings into a leadership culture that is truly lived in practice.".

The Bundeswehr urgently needs additional personnel and has been actively recruiting women. However, the study's findings are unlikely to make attracting more female recruits any easier. Women remain significantly underrepresented across nearly all branches of the armed forces.

This article was originally written in German.

The White and Sky Blues are the only team in Spain's top flight yet to triumph this term, and they are in danger of becoming cut adrift at the bottom of the La Liga table.

Osasuna boast a record of three wins, three draws and six defeats from their 12 league matches this season, with 12 points leaving them in 16th spot in the division.

Jagoba Arrasate's side entered the November international break off the back of a 1-1 draw with Athletic Bilbao, but they did start the month with a 2-1 loss to Deportivo La Coruna.

As a result, there is plenty of room for improvement during the current campaign, but consistency has been a problem in the opening months of the season.

Osasuna have only won seven of their previous 32 matches against Malaga in all competitions, suffering 12 defeats in the process, while there have also been 13 draws.

Malaga are winless in their last four games against Osasuna, though, and they have beaten Sunday's opponents just once since April 2013.

This match will mark the first fixture between the two teams since March 2019, when Osasuna recorded a 2-1 victory, while they also won 2-1 in the reverse game in the same season.

Malaga are rock bottom of the La Liga table, only picking up five points from their opening 12 matches of the season, boasting a record of zero wins, five draws and seven defeats.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Metabolic disorders such as diabetes mellitus are global health crises driven by metabolic imbalance, chronic inflammation and dysfunction of the neuroimmune axis1,2,3.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Metabolic disorders such as diabetes mellitus are global health crises driven by metabolic imbalance, chronic inflammation and dysfunction of the neuroimmune axis1,2,3. Electroceuticals targeting the autonomic nervous system have shown anti-inflammatory effects, yet existing systems lack the metabolic interoceptive feedback to fully restore immune–metabolic homeostasis4,5,6,7,8,9. Here we report an artificial neuroimmune axis (NeuroAxis) as a closed-loop immunomodulatory therapy for treating metabolic diseases. Analogous to its biological counterpart, NeuroAxis is solely powered by endogenous glucose, operating without batteries or wireless power transfer. It emulates the vagal reflex through closed-loop neuromodulation with metabolic interoceptive feedback. In a rat model of type 1 diabetes, NeuroAxis promotes the recovery of insulin-producing pancreatic β-cells and reduces inflammatory immune responses; in a rat model of type 2 diabetes, it drives macrophage remodelling and reduces systemic chronic inflammation. In both models, NeuroAxis restores glucose tolerance, improves insulin sensitivity and normalizes glycaemic control, with therapeutic effects persisting after treatment cessation. Our artificial neuroimmune axis promotes substantial advances in treating metabolic disorders and represents a general approach for autonomously regulating interorgan communication, central to homeostasis and pathophysiology.

Sources indicate that logic control of NeuroAxis during closed-loop glucose-responsive neuromodulation. The NeuroAxis-mediated VNS is triggered only after the glucose level exceeds a threshold of five consecutive readings. Once the stimulation condition is met, the system delivers biphasic electrical pulses for 3 min.

Recent findings suggest that this blog is now closed. Read below for a roundup of news from or pertaining to Germany on November 12, 2026:.

Luxury automaker Mercedes-Benz is halting investment at its facilities in Germany, a board members revealed on Thursday.

Mercedes-Benz is "forced to examine, in concrete and detailed terms, which sites in Germany we can still afford to maintain," board of management member Britta Seeger said in an interview published on the tech giant's intranet.

Germany's major IG Metall trade union has enabled the possibility of longer warning strikes amid difficult negotiations for industrial employees.

"The board of IG Metall has pave the way for 24-hour warning strikes in the metalworking and electrical industry," the union noted on Thursday.

The union accuses employers of intransigence after three rounds of negotiations without clear progress.

On Wednesday, regional chapters appealed for authorization for full-day warning strikes — the last step before a full union vote and an indefinite labor dispute.

In a recent development, "This escalation is completely excessive and counterproductive," Udo Dinglreiter, the president of the employers' umbrella organization, Gesamtmetall, said. He said that hundreds of thousands of jobs could be at risk.

IG Metall's first chairperson Christiane Benner countered that "the employers want to turn this round of collective bargaining into a dispute over principles." Another union official remarked they were offering what amounted to a real-terms pay cut rather than seeking solutions.

IG Metall is calling for a 5% pay increase and other improved conditions for some 3.7 million workers starting in November, while employers have offered a one-off payment in 2027 coupled with a 1.3% increase starting in the summer of 2028.

The union estimates that around 464,000 employees took part in the initial wave of warning strikes that were limited to periods of hours, rather than full days.

Employers argue that they're treading a difficult line between trying not to cut jobs and meeting calls for improved pay amid widespread industrial sector layoffs in Germany in recent years.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

'Tis the season, already. Preparations are underway around Germany and in several cities, Christmas markets are opening to the public.

Some markets are already open in Essen and in Hamburg, Duisburg's opens on Thursday, and Cologne's follows a day later.

The coupons.de website has sought to track the planned prices for mulled wine or Glühwein as the markets open their doors nationwide.

The bad news? These prices are rising like so many others. The better news? The year-on-year increase is actually smaller than overall inflation figures, at around 1%.

Sources indicate that on average, a cup is liable to set you back around €4.60 (roughly $5.10). Not entirely surprisingly, Munich tops the nationwide pricing chart, with the price peaking at €7. Other sites nationwide tend not to have the gall even to charge 6 euros.

Bargain hunters determined to get the best value mulled wine will need to venture deep into the center of Germany — hardly its core tourist hub — to find the lowest prices starting at around €3.50.

Deposits for the cup, the "Pfand," are also only going in one direction, and in the meantime range from €1 all the way up to €5. But there's a strong argument, particularly with the better designs or after a memorable trip, that this can be money well spent as a memento!

Police in the Emsland region in the northwest near the border to the Netherlands have reported a major fire in a complex of residential and commercial buildings in Papenburg.

The fire broke out on Wednesday afternoon, police stated the following morning, causing damages worth "at least €10 million ($11 million)." Several hundred emergency services personnel were deployed.

"Based on current findings, the fire broke out in the sauna area of a gym facility on site, and promptly spread to further parts of the complex of buildings," police wrote.

Two men were in the sauna at the time and initially tried to douse the flames but without success.

Police said the buildings were evacuated as the fire spread, with some surrounding buildings also being cleared as a precaution because of possible smoke-related dangers.

Several people were injured, police stated, including the two men in the sauna area suffering mild burns and suspected smoke inhalation sickness. They were treated in a nearby hospital but soon discharged.

In a recent development, "There were also injuries among the first responders," police wrote. "Four police officers, two firefighters and members of the rescue teams suffered mild injuries, particularly via smoke inhalation.".

The fire was only extinguished late on Wednesday night, several hours after it started. The area is sealed off, with possible risks of damaged buildings collapsing. Police have also released investigations into the fire's cause, but mentioned that at present, the area was not safe for that work to start at full scale.

Germany's largest credit bureau Creditreform has published its "2026 Debtors' Atlas.".

It finds that 10.16% of German adults, or 7.36 million people, exhibit at least the early warning signs of excessive debt. A year ago the ratio was 9.74%.

According to recent reports, "The financial situation of private consumers has further deteriorated," Patrik-Ludwig Hantzsch, Creditreform's head of economic research, noted. "In particular, the sharply increased living costs, energy costs and housing costs are straining expenditures.".

Hantzsch said employment was also becoming an issue once more, saying "above all, well-paid jobs in manufacturing industries have been cut back in large numbers in recent months.".

The report also highlights rising cases of signs of excessive debt prior to legal action being taken, such as payment reminders or warnings being sent, saying "consumers are taking on more credit-financed expenditures — increasingly also for smaller purchases — at simultaneously rising interest rates.".

A larger share of men than women have excessive debts, perpetuating a longstanding trend.

People around the middle of their working lives, aged 30-39 and 40-49, are most likely to be affected — but the cohort with the fastest-rising share of people with excessive debts are young adults below the age of 30.

Bremen, Berlin, Saxony-Anhalt and North Rhine-Westphalia were among the states with the highest rates of excess debts, while the wealthy and fiscally conservative states of Bavaria and Baden-Württemberg had the lowest levels.

Germany's main DAX stock market index has cleared the 27,000-point mark for the first time in its history in morning trading.

It climbed by around 1.3% in order to pass the milestone.

A combination of some positive outlook data from major companies, not least engineering giant Siemens, and the falling oil prices of recent days have helped fuel the uptick.

Siemens' shares had risen by almost 5%, to just over €291 (around $323) each, helping to spur on the gains and making the manufacturer the morning's top performer.

Despite several years of low growth and recession in the German economy, the DAX, like many Western indices, is now trading twice as high as it was prior to the COVID pandemic.

Hundreds of police officers searched apartments and meeting sites for the biker group "Gremium MC" in the southwestern state of Baden-Württemberg early on Thursday.

The state interior ministry said the operation was part of a move to outlaw three sub-chapters of the group, the ones based in Böblingen and Leonberg, as well as the "Gremium MC Chapter Nomads Bosphorus Türkiye.".

This last group was highlighted as a meaningful part of Gremium MC by security officials. It describes itself on Facebook as a great example that "people of different cultures and faiths can be strong together," featuring images of men posing with knives and other weapons.

Gremium MC prominently incorporates into its iconography the symbol of the Prussian military medal for exceptional valor, the Iron Cross, which was discontinued after World War I, reintroduced by Adolf Hitler during World War II, and then scrapped for good.

State Interior Minister Manuel Hagel was expected to make further comments later in the day in Ludwigsburg.

Gremium MC is deemed an "outlaw motorcycle gang" in Baden-Württemberg's latest security report, a term used for biker groups that do not recognize the state monopoly on the use of force and are often tied to organized crime.

"Extortion, drug dealing and pimping in particular tend to be part of their activities," state authorities say.

Baden-Württemberg counts 154 biker chapters in the state with around 2,000 members.

Founded in 1972 in Mannheim, various chapters of Gremium MC across the country have faced legal challenges in recent years. In 2021, another chapter in the southwest, Gremium MC Southgate in Heidelberg, was outlawed on suspicion of organized crime activity.

Police in Hanover reported early on Thursday that three men were injured by an unknown driver in a car in the nearby town of Ronneberg.

One person sustained severe injuries in the incident late on Wednesday, police remarked.

Two of the wounded were taken to a nearby hospital while the other could be cared for at the scene.

Police said the driver fled the scene and that a search operation was ongoing. Authorities were also still investigating a potential motive for the apparent attack.

Today's updates start with a focus between the southwestern Kurpfalz and Swabian regions, where police have launched major morning raids against a biker gang.

The state Interior Ministry in Baden Württemberg has outlawed three of its chapters. Hundreds of police officers mobilized in the early hours of the morning.

The major IG Metall trade union is planning further strikes in the carmaking sector and other metalworking industries, with an announcement anticipated later in the day.

To the north, near Hanover, police report an apparent car attack injuring three men overnight.

It has been revealed that and in the spirit of offering the public service journalism people are truly thirsting for, we'll have some info on the average and localized pricing of mulled wine or Glühwein at Christmas markets this year, as the early birds start to open their doors to visitors. (Yes, already!).

Stay tuned for updates on all this and anything else of note in or pertaining to Germany as the day progresses.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 20 Nov 2026 13:39.

Second-placed Brighton & Hove Albion travel to face Hull City on Sunday as Fabian Hurzeler's side look to extend their impressive run of form in the clubs' first-ever Premier League meeting.

Sergej Jakirovic's Tigers sit 13th after 10 matches and three points clear of the relegation zone, having gone eight league games without a victory despite remaining unbeaten on home soil this season.

Conversely, the Seagulls arrive full of confidence after recording consecutive top-flight wins over Manchester City and Brentford, boasting six clean sheets across their last seven league outings.

Here, Sports Mole takes a closer look at the head-to-head record and past meetings between Hull and Brighton.

Nearly 67 years have passed since Hull City and Brighton & Hove Albion first locked horns - a November 1959 Division Two clash that ended in a 3-1 victory for the Tigers - and there have now been 51 competitive meetings between the two clubs in all competitions.

The Seagulls hold the bragging rights when it comes to overall victories with 22, while Hull have claimed 15 wins of their own and another 14 contests have seen the spoils shared.

Remarkably, none of those 51 encounters have taken place in the Premier League, with every previous battle arriving in the Football League or the FA Cup, and the two sides have not crossed paths since a goalless Championship stalemate in East Yorkshire in February 2016.

Recent clashes between the pair have been notably tight, low-scoring affairs, with none of their last nine meetings across all competitions settled by more than a single goal and three ending 0-0.

During the 2015-16 campaign, both clubs collected a narrow 1-0 victory on home soil - Brighton prevailing in the Championship in September 2015 before Hull gained revenge in the FA Cup four months later - prior to that goalless draw in February.

Indeed, home advantage has heavily dictated this fixture in the modern era, as Hull are unbeaten in their last six home games against Brighton across all competitions - winning four and keeping five clean sheets - since suffering a 2-0 Division Three defeat in October 2000.

Conversely, the Tigers have endured a miserable record on the South Coast, failing to win any of their last 22 visits to Brighton since recording their sole away triumph in this fixture - a 2-1 Division Three success - way back in August 1965.

Brighton built much of their overall head-to-head lead during a dominant spell in the late 1980s and 1990s, rattling off four straight victories between October 1989 and April 1991 before later embarking on a nine-match unbeaten run from April 1993 to December 1996.

That sequence included the Seagulls' biggest-ever win in this matchup, a resounding 4-0 Division Two triumph in March 1996, while they also completed a comfortable league double over Hull with 2-0 and 3-0 victories in the 2000-01 Division Three season.

Hull's most emphatic triumph came in the highest-scoring meeting between the two sides, a 5-2 Division Two victory in December 1988, while they also put three unanswered goals past Brighton in March 1997.

The two teams have also collided five times in the FA Cup, with Brighton winning the first two ties in January 1985 (1-0) and January 1986 (3-2) before Hull turned the tide by edging a 2-1 replay victory in February 2014 following a 1-1 draw and claiming that 1-0 success in January 2016.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 17:05 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 17:05 EST, 17 November 2026.

After a thrilling international break that saw England record an historic 3-2 win over Spain our focus returns to the Premier League.

And what a weekend we have coming up. Old gaffers in fresh colours, fierce rivalries and some seminal fixtures in the context of the whole season.

With so much to look forward to this weekend, Daily Mail Sport looks over the key reasons to be excited for the return of the world's most electric league.

After a flying start to the campaign Manchester City have begun to run into serious problems under Enzo Maresca and have lost their last three Premier League games on the trot.

And after a particularly humiliating defeat away to Nottingham Forest, who hadn't scored at home before the Cityzens' visit, Maresca and his squad will be desperate for three points especially with champions Arsenal now six points clear.

Industry observers note that city have a good opportunity to turn things around, though, as they host a Fulham side who have endured a terrible run of form against Saturday’s opponents. In fact, the Cottagers have failed to beat City in their last 20 Premier League meetings - a run stretching back 14 years.

But, as ever in the Premier League, nothing is guaranteed and Alvaro Arbeloa’s side are showing promising signs - having enjoyed an unbeaten run in their past four games.

Enzo Maresca's side started in scintillating form but have lost their last three games.

Bonfire night has only just passed but don’t be surprised to see fireworks in west London on Saturday as old rivals Chelsea and Leeds do battle at Stamford Bridge.

After comfortably surviving in their returning year last season, Leeds have kicked on and have quietly emerged as a strong contender for European football. Daniel Farke’s side at the moment sit ninth, just two points off fifth place Chelsea.

It has been revealed that the Blues on the other hand have endured a stuttering, frustrating start to the season. Xabi Alonso’s heralded front three of Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro have showcased their terrifying attacking prowess, but the Blues boss’ mystifying tinkering, plus inconsistent performances, has seen his side drop points against Spurs and Sunderland.

However, form will go out of the window as this rivalry - 55 years in the making - is reignited.

Chelsea will be hoping for a repeat of their 6-3 win over Leeds in the league cup this season but Daniel Farke's men will not be as easy to get past in the league.

After Pierre Sage’s dismal start to life in south London, the Crystal Palace board did not hang around and gave the Frenchman the boot after just five months in charge.

And the Eagles have made sure to replace him with someone who has Premier League pedigree, Thomas Frank.

Now while recent memories of the Danish gaffer are almost universally negative it is easy to forget that before his calamitous stint at Tottenham he worked wonders down in west London for Brentford.

And he has every chance of doing the same at Selhurst Park. The job will be far from easy as his fresh team right now sit rock bottom of the league, but considering Frank’s high pressing and wide set playstyle, Palace’s squad looks a good fit for the Dane.

His first game back will be a tough test, away to Frank Lampard’s resurgent Coventry, but Frank - and the travelling Palace contingent - will be hoping for a new manager bounce in the east Midlands.

Thomas Frank returns to London to take charge of a struggling Crystal Palace side.

With City faltering and Liverpool and Chelsea failing to hit their stride, the Premier League title race is fast developing into a one-horse competition - and Mikel Arteta will not care one bit.

The Spaniard’s well-oiled machine looks near impossible to stop but as Brighton proved before the last international break, they are not infallible and are set for a tough test returning from the latest break.

The Gunners travel to St James’ Park to take on Newcastle in what promises to be another thriller.

In years past the trip up north has proved to be a banana skin for Arsenal and Arteta, losing four out of their last six games there.

In a recent development, however, Newcastle fans fear their side are fast becoming a fading force and the trip to the North East isn’t perhaps as intimidating as it once was. After all, the Gunners picked up a stoppage time win there last season on their way to the title.

Mikel Arteta's side are hitting their stride but face a tough test at St James' Park.

The surprise package of the season has undoubtedly been Fabian Hurzeler’s high-flying Seagulls who are perched in second place after 10 excellent games.

Recent findings suggest that they remain the only side to have beaten the champions Arsenal and are the league’s top scorers by five goals. They are efficient, fun to watch and have scored a plethora of absolute scorchers this season, but the question on everyone’s lips is: can they keep it up?

History would suggest that overperforming teams tend to settle into the pack after a fast start, and end up battling it out for a coveted spot in a lesser European competition.

In a recent development, but somehow this year it feels different. Brighton appear to have everything they might need to maintain this form and seriously challenge for a Champions League place.

Recent findings suggest that the squad has depth and dynamism with a littany of players boasting youthful exuberance, sprinkled with the experience of the ever-reliable Lewis Dunk and the resurgent Pascal Gross. Crucially, they have a top, motivated manager hellbent on breaking the mould.

Upon return from the break Brighton travel a stubborn Hull side, for their first ever top flight meeting between the two sides.

Brighton have been truly sensational in the opening ten games but can they keep this up going into the notoriously tough winter period.

It seems that after nearly 18 months at Liverpool Florian Wirtz is finally beginning to perform.

After a dismal first year in England in which he only registered nine goals and assists in 33 Premier League games the £116million man is starting to rediscover the form that earned him that valuation.

He enjoyed possibly his best performance in a red shirt just before the break, scoring and assisting in a 3-1 away win against Crystal Palace, and has taken that form into his international performances.

The attacking midfielder got one against Serbia in a routine 3-1 win as well as netting a brace in a 5-0 drubbing of the Netherlands - with one of his strikes an absolute pearler.

The Kop will hope this is the precursor to Wirtz seriously hitting form in the Premier League but the 23-year-old still has a lot to do before he repays the money Liverpool paid for him last year.

Florian Wirtz looks in the mood after a couple of excellent performances for Germany under ex-Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp.

There is no skirting around the biggest story of the international break - the psychodrama at Manchester United. The two-week break saw the Red Devils wave goodbye to Michael Carrick and say hello to Mauricio Pochettino, hoping the incoming Argentinian will inspire a much-needed turnaround.

After an emotional press conference in which he said goodbye to the US men’s national team, who he has managed for the last two years, the former Spurs and Chelsea boss is tasked with getting his new club out of the relegation places and finding some much-needed stability.

And it will be a baptism of fire for the 54-year-old, who takes his strugglers to the Anfield cauldron on Sunday, to face a Liverpool side who will have to travel to Anfield, to face a Liverpool side already 10 points ahead.

Factor in the history and rivalry this fixture holds and we are in for a cracker on Merseyside. The smart money would be on Liverpool but as we have seen so many times before a new manager bounce can transform a team in a matter of hours.

And that is all he will have to prepare his charges for their trip to Liverpool - with the new boss landing in Manchester on Wednesday morning to begin work straightaway. Welcome back, Pochettino.

Poch is back and this time in red but he will have his work cut out for him managing a dysfunctional United side right now sat in 18th.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that whether in the form of crumbly rock, odorless gas or slick black liquid, ancient organic compounds have powered the flourishing of modern life.
  • The collective term refers to coal, oil and natural gas — a group of energy sources that contain carbon and hydrogen.
  • Sources indicate that they started life hundreds of millions of years ago as living plants and animals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that whether in the form of crumbly rock, odorless gas or slick black liquid, ancient organic compounds have powered the flourishing of modern life. But now they threaten to make the planet unlivable for many plants, animals and humans.

The collective term refers to coal, oil and natural gas — a group of energy sources that contain carbon and hydrogen.

Sources indicate that they started life hundreds of millions of years ago as living plants and animals. When they died, they sank to the bottom of oceans and swamps where they decomposed under layers of sediment.

Over time, this matter was buried deeper and deeper into the earth, subjecting it to increasing pressure and heat which changed its chemical composition. Plants and trees transformed into coal, whereas microscopic plankton and algae became oil and — if the heat and pressure increased further — gas.

Today fossil fuels can be found in the earth's crust all around the world although some countries, such as the US, Saudi Arabia and Russia, have bigger reserves than others.

Coal, found in underground coal beds, is extracted by mining, whereas oil and gas, found in reservoirs beneath the land and ocean, are accessed by drilling.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Since the early 19th Century, when the discovery and exploitation of fossil fuel reserves powered the Industrial Revolution, our use of them has skyrocketed, increasing eight-fold since 1950.

Today they provide 80% of our energy needs through heating, electricity generation and transport.

We transform them into energy either by burning them directly in furnaces that warm up our homes and businesses, or in power plants to heat water into steam which then generates electricity. When it comes to transport, crude oil is refined into a range of products such as diesel, gasoline and kerosene that are burned in the engines of automobiles, airplanes and ships. Natural gas is also sometimes compressed for use in cars and buses.

But fossil fuels are also essential to a huge range of products including steel, formed using a coal-derived material called coke, and plastic, which is produced by refining and processing crude oil and gas.

Recent findings suggest that fossil fuels are by far the biggest contributors to climate change. When burned to power our modern lives, they emit carbon dioxide (CO2) into Earth's atmosphere, trapping heat and causing temperatures to rise.

With 2025 officially one of the warmest years on record, the impact of these emissions is being felt around the world. Hotter temperatures are causing polar ice caps to melt and creating the conditions for extreme weather events — such as floods, drought, wildfires and storms — to become more intense and frequent.

In a recent development, scientists stress the need to limit global warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) to avoid unleashing the most catastrophic impacts of climate change. That was laid out in the 2015 Paris Agreement. At the moment, there are 194 parties to the agreement, but progress has been too slow, and overall emissions continue to rise.

Three years after countries agreed at the UN climate conference in Dubai COP28 to transition away from coal, oil and gas. After the previous COP in Brazil failed to reach a consensus on a concrete plan, Brazil has now presented a roadmap aimed at turning that promise into national plans.

"It is long past time to stop treating the transition away from fossil fuels as taboo or intractable," United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Saikat Mandal | 20 Nov 2026 13:41.

Arsenal have reportedly joined Real Madrid in the race to sign Bayern Munich winger Michael Olise.

The 24-year-old joined Bayern in the summer of 2024 from Crystal Palace and has established himself as one of the finest wingers in European football.

The Frenchman has scored 54 goals and provided 61 assists in 122 appearances, although even those phenomenal numbers do not fully reflect what he brings to the Bayern side.

During the summer transfer window, Real Madrid were heavily linked with a move for Olise, but Bayern made it clear that the winger was not for sale at any price.

Bayern have reportedly placed a £265m valuation on Olise, who is under contract at the Allianz Arena until 2029.

However, club CEO Herbert Hainer has made it clear that no such asking price has been set for the player, whom they want to keep for many years to come.

According to Christian Falk, Arsenal are among the clubs interested in Olise, although it could prove difficult for the Gunners to prise him away from Bayern.

If Olise does decide to leave Munich, a move to La Liga could make more sense, having already experienced life in the Premier League.

There is also a significant gap between Olise's earnings and those of Harry Kane at Bayern, and the German club are expected to do everything in their power to convince the winger to sign a new contract.

According to recent reports, the Bild journalist stated: "Every club has Michael Olise on their shortlist. There’s a lot of respect for Arsenal, but there are some really big players at the table, like Real Madrid.

"Olise has already played in the Premier League, so I strongly suspect a move to La Liga would be the next logical step were he to look for a move away from Munich.

"That all noted, Bayern Munich have proven that big personal awards like the Ballon d’Or can still be won at FC Bayern. So, that’s the hope of the club and they’ll do everything in their power to keep Olise at the Allianz Arena.".

Olise could still be tempted to stay at Bayern after seeing his club teammate Harry Kane win the Ballon d'Or this year.

A move to a more competitive league could appeal to the Frenchman, while he may also want to join a club where his chances of winning the Champions League are high.

Bayern have not set an asking price for Olise and could demand a staggering fee, with paying such an amount likely to be nothing short of madness.

Arsenal arguably need a right winger who can provide reliable cover for Bukayo Saka rather than a player of Olise's calibre, who would expect to be a guaranteed starter if he made the move to the Emirates Stadium.

By Ben Knapton | 20 Nov 2026 14:06, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 14:06.

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola has confirmed a quadruple injury boost for his side ahead of Sunday's blockbuster Premier League battle with Manchester United at Anfield.

The Reds have the honour of hosting Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge of the Red Devils, in which they will endeavour to improve on a paltry record of just one win from five home matches in the 2026-27 top flight.

Liverpool maintained their excellent away form by beating Crystal Palace 3-1 before the international break, but Dominik Szoboszlai emerged as an injury worry following the Selhurst Park success.

The midfielder nevertheless joined up with Hungary for the November international break and played the full 90 in both of their Nations League games against Georgia and Northern Ireland, supplying two assists against the former.

Szoboszlai was managing a knee problem during his time with the Magyars, but speaking to the media on Friday, Iraola affirmed that the 26-year-old will be fine for Sunday's main event.

"He's in a good place, he's playing normally, he was not even strapped today so he's fine yes," Iraola responded when asked if Szoboszlai was still being carefully looked after.

As well as confirming Szoboszlai's availability, Iraola delivered positive updates on the Dutch trio of Ryan Gravenberch, Jeremie Frimpong and Virgil van Dijk.

The latter withdrew from the Netherlands squad for the November window due to an unspecified fitness problem, while Gravenberch and Frimpong were both absent from the win over Palace.

Frimpong sustained a hamstring injury against Brentford in October and has missed Liverpool's last six games in all competitions, while Gravenberch has been dealing with a minor heal fracture.

However, all three are in line to feature against old rivals Man United, as Iraola added: "If everything goes to proposal they should be available for the game.

Recent findings suggest that "Gravenberch, it's a matter of pain, he's managing but he's been training the last two days. Jeremie is recovering the same. We've introduced him with the rest of the group, and Virgil is fine to go.".

Should all of Szoboszlai, Van Dijk, Gravenberch and Frimpong make the cut, Liverpool's only remaining concerns are the long-term trio of Conor Bradley, Giovanni Leoni and Hugo Ekitike.

The latter is still a while away from making a full recovery from an Achilles injury, but Leoni and Bradley have returned to team training as they close in on returns from serious knee injuries.

However, Iraola confirmed that neither defender will be in the squad on Sunday, adding: "The international break was the best moment to introduce them slowly, they've started doing things with the team. They are still not available, but it's very good news and I hope they can play in some weeks.".

Liverpool sit fourth in the Premier League table with 18 points from their opening 10 games, but they have won just two of their last nine matches against Man Utd.

By Darren Plant | 20 Nov 2026 14:08.

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has revealed that Joao Pedro remains unavailable for Saturday's Premier League fixture against Leeds United.

However, despite suggesting that he was dealing with fitness issues while on international duty with Ecuador, Moises Caicedo has been declared fit.

The Blues return to action this weekend sitting in fifth place in the Premier League table, yet Alonso is under pressure to deliver after four defeats in 10 top-flight matches.

Pedro has been sidelined since the October 17 game at Everton with a thigh injury, and it remains unclear when he will return.

Speaking at a press conference on Friday, Alonso stated that two players had been passed fit, while three players in total are still ruled out.

Recent findings suggest that when quizzed on Pedro, the Spaniard told reporters: "Not yet. He's not fit yet to train with the team.

"He's not going to be available for Leeds. We need to see game by game how he's feeling.".

Alonso went on to say that Maxence Lacroix, who suffered a hamstring injury versus Liverpool on October 28, was in a similar situation to Pedro, while Jorrel Hato remains out with a back problem.

Nevertheless, as well as Caicedo being passed fit, Josh Acheampong will be back in the squad after missing one Premier League game and two England Under-21 matches with a minor glitch.

Meanwhile, Alonso has added that Reece James is still "some weeks away" from returning from a knee injury that required surgery.

However, despite not being back in contention this week, Alonso revealed that Jamie Gittens is training with the first-team squad after six weeks out with an ankle injury.

Jensen Huang: Spy row, affairs leave Nvidia without its rockstar CEO

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia's board met late Wednesday to decide on CEO Jensen Huang's future as reports emerged of other extramarital affairs — this time with employees.
  • In a statement issued on Thursday, the world's most valuable chip supplier said Huang was resigning as President, CEO and board member, effective immediately.
  • The firm added that current Vice President and Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Colette Kress would become interim CEO.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia's board met late Wednesday to decide on CEO Jensen Huang's future as reports emerged of other extramarital affairs — this time with employees.

In a statement issued on Thursday, the world's most valuable chip supplier said Huang was resigning as President, CEO and board member, effective immediately.

The firm added that current Vice President and Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Colette Kress would become interim CEO.

Under Nvidia's bylaws, Huang can be removed "with or without cause" by a majority vote of its 11 directors.

The New York Times first reported that the 63-year-old Huang had an affair with a senior Nvidia executive who reported directly to him.

Later Thursday, Reuters news agency alleged an intimate relationship between Huang and a second employee, citing unidentified sources.

Those revelations emerged just three days after Huang admitted a relationship with a Chinese woman, whom United States intelligence agencies believe was spying for China. The woman, Alice Huang — no relation — is a former executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based cloud computing firm that runs artificial intelligence (AI) data centers across Southeast Asia and is a major client of Nvidia.

The US government is investigating the startup on suspicion that it secretly sent some of its Nvidia chips to China, violating Washington's curbs on high-end semiconductors.

Those advanced Nvidia processors ‌are ​used to train and run the large AI models behind chatbots and other generative AI products.

Megaspeed denies the allegations and on Thursday pledged to cooperate with US investigators. Huang, the alleged spy, has been barred from entering Singapore and Taiwan — a key chipmaking island.

While Nvidia's board backed its CEO after the first scandal emerged, market watchers believe the second caused too much reputational damage to one of the world's top three companies by market value.

According to The Wall Street Journal, Huang doesn't believe in formal succession planning, so with little notice, Nvidia appointed CFO Kress as interim CEO.

Bloomberg reported Wednesday that Nvidia’s board is working with advisers to identify potential permanent successors.

Kress, other senior Nvidia executives and members of Huang's own family have been mooted as replacements. The family members include his daughter Madison, a senior director of product marketing, and his son Spencer, who at the moment works in the firm's robotics division.

According to recent reports, rumors also abound over a longer-term solution. On India's CNBC-TV18, Jeffrey Sonnenfeld from the Yale School of Management floated former Apple CEO Tim Cook and ex-Google CEO Eric Schmidt.

US President Donald Trump also backed Cook on social media, writing: "A Legend replaces a Legend.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The scandals have certainly hit Nvidia's market value. Since the first extramarital affair emerged on Sunday, the chipmaker's market capitalization has fallen by well over $600 billion to $4.2 trillion.

In a recent development, nvidia shares were down more than 9% in premarket trading Thursday, after dropping by 10% earlier this week. Some analysts expect the stock price to struggle in the short term.

Nvidia stock hit all-time highs just a month ago as US technology giants continued to announce billions in spending on AI infrastructure.

Demand for Nvidia's advanced chips is so high, however, that many market analysts expect little impact on near-term sales.

"While Jensen [Huang] is the heart and lungs of the Nvidia story…the company and its leading-edge GPU technology will go on and [his departure] does not change the entrenched position Nvidia has in the AI Revolution chip arms race," stated Dan Ives, a partner, senior managing director and tech analyst at Yorkville Ives, a US-based merchant bank.

Analysts see the biggest long-term risk in strategy and execution. After all, Huang was the leader who picked which ideas Nvidia should bet heavily on and got the whole company behind them.

His sudden exit is also seen as highly disruptive to the chip designer's strong relationships with AI hyperscalers, Taiwanese chip producer TSMC and foreign governments — especially China.

Huang was Nvidia's main lobbyist on US chip export rules and persuaded US President Donald Trump to ease some curbs on China last year.

Huang is often called a rockstar CEO for his leather jackets instead of suits.

Like Elon Musk of Tesla and SpaceX, he was also seen as a key-person risk as Nvidia’s public image, strategic direction and technical decisions became closely tied to him.

Huang steered the tech giant for more than three decades and was also respected for his hands-on involvement in product architecture and engineering decisions.

He also insisted on a flat management structure, with around 60 executives reporting directly to him.

Huang has run the manufacturer so tightly around his own technical judgment and product decisions that investors may have little sense of how it would function without him.

At the same time, Nvidia is no longer the startup Huang founded in 1993. The company has built deep expertise in chip design and software, creating a durable moat that helps protect its huge profits, which topped $120.1 billion last year.

Some analysts argue that its central role in the AI hardware buildout makes it less dependent on Huang’s day-to-day input.

China is quickly playing catch-up with the US in the global race for AI dominance.

While Chinese AI models have lagged behind the likes of ChatGPT and Claude, recent updates from DeepSeek, Alibaba and Moonshot have closed much of the gap on benchmark tests and often beat US rivals on cost and speed.

Beijing is also investing heavily in domestic chips and data centers to reduce reliance on US hardware.

The US has curbed exports to China of Nvidia's most advanced AI chips.

However, this move has only slowed the pace of China's AI ambitions.

Reuters reported Thursday that Chinese AI firms are now trying to rent Nvidia-powered computing capacity at data centers outside China, amid fears the US could further tighten restrictions on advanced chips.

Also Thursday, Beijing accused the US of using the Nvidia spying claims as a pretext to impose a technological "blockade" on China.

The concern is likely to dominate talks next week between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping at the APEC gathering in Shenzhen in southern China.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that I suppose I’m mildly curious as to whether Viktor Gyokeres’ performance on Wednesday will see him keep his place up front.
